items.title: Soulframe Preview – Digital Extremes’ Warframe follow-up is ready to rule
items.summary: Digital Extremes’ journey through more than three decades of game development has been one marked with challenges, successes and a few failures, but in
items.content:
Digital Extremes’ journey through more than three decades of game development has been one marked with challenges, successes and a few failures, but in 2026 the company is arguably in the best position it’s ever been in. Warframe , its sci-fi ninja opus, is enjoying its best year – 14 years in from its original release, that feat is truly remarkable – and all the while it’s quietly tinkering away with its sword-and-sorcery follow-up, Soulframe .

Up till now, you’ve been able to experience the closed alpha test Soulframe Prelude only by invitation, but on November 6th they’re finally entering open beta. For the past three years, the team have maintained an open dialogue with its players and community, helping to build something that already feels pretty special. Now, though, it feels as though they’re ready to take the final steps towards the game’s full release, and, frankly, I couldn’t be more excited.

The game’s gloriously poetic opening sets an evocative tone, showcasing the emotional depth and poignancy that underlies Soulframe’s setting and outlook. Here, the Scottish narrator broadly leads your character development, but in the most unusual way, choosing traits for your mother as she cradles you in her arms. These are then inherited by your avatar as you meet them, bound and battered by an unknown Ode knight, before you’re dumped face-first into a pool wearing nothing but your grubby white underpants. Oh, and an intricate locked gauntlet that covers your entire arm. Seems odd, no?

You’re an Envoy, marked by the distinctive blue arm that lies beneath that gauntlet. As Soulframe leads you into its early systems, your next major milestone is choosing your Pact, with Courage, Grace or Spirit giving you the option between a melee, ranged or magic starting class, and then tailoring your equipment as you see fit. I was really interested in playing a ranged character, but decided to opt for a melee build, becoming a devotee of Tethren for my first time experiencing the game. You’ve got a batch of swords to choose from, and I went for a cool-looking sword and shield combo, with the ability to throw your shield and have it return to you, very much like a certain bearded God of War.

This is where it all begins. You’re dropped into the open world island of Midreth, part of the wider world of Alca, with a small number of enemies lurking in nearby hamlets, while you get to grips with the game’s combat. Despite whatever the name Soulframe might suggest, this is not a Souls-like. Combat is approachable, with a satisfying and rewarding parry window that lets you feel powerful without these opening moments feeling like a complete walkover. Depending on the Pact you’ve chosen, you have three different abilities to utilise, though only one of these is unlocked at the opening.

Where things suddenly get more difficult is when you come across a group of Ode. A batch of different warriors and machinery suddenly make things much more fraught, forcing you to focus attacks, dodge, block and parry, while trying to control the space and avoid ranged attacks at the same time. It feels excellent, giving you lots to manage, while giving weight and strength to each of your blows. That’s then further complicated by the addition of Combat Arts, both weapon specific and more generic, such as Smite, which you can sometimes leverage to strike at an enemy’s soul.

The Ode have a penchant for capturing cute and furry creatures, and through the opening hours you’ll relish saving deer, rabbits and squirrels from their nefarious clutches, while seeking to purify and heal the land that the Ode seem intent on destroying. I don’t know why, but it really reminded me of Sonic the Hedgehog saving animals from Robotnik – in the best way possible. We’ll have to see if there’s a spiky blue armour set to complete the vibes.

Through the opening, you meet Orlick the Bicameral, a ghostly writer with a hooded baby on his shoulder that occasionally whispers in his ear. His ephemeral form is searching for his quill, and once you return it, he’ll join you in the Nightfold, your home base that sits in a watery pocket dimension. He serves as your spirit guide when you’re exploring, providing spots of exposition and insight, before using his writing prowess to record your greatest deeds, though it is, in reality, just a framing device that gives you a list of secondary tasks to complete to grab some additional spoils.

His design is indicative of Digital Extremes’ idiosyncratic outlook, and just like Warframe, there’s nothing that looks or feels quite like this. From the different Ode warriors through creatures like Avakot, a leafy little chap with allergies, to the Torment Stag, the first corrupted boss, it does skew closer to the creations of FromSoftware, but there’s still an overarching individuality and slightly off-kilter outlook that infuses the art direction throughout.

That’s especially true when it comes to the armour sets you can equip; they don’t carry the same wholly alien look of its predecessor, but they definitely don’t adhere to your traditional Western medieval fantasy, drawing instead on Celtic mythology and iconography, wrapped with a tinge of Warframe’s sci-fi trappings.

Soulframe looks fantastic. The fact that this is considered an early build is astounding, and it already feels, at least at the outset, like a AAA action game. The quality of the visuals and the level design is intricate, particularly when it comes to exploring the Undercity dungeons that lurk beneath the beautiful arable fantasy, and through the opening hours you’ll repeatedly marvel at what beauty the DE team have brought to bear.

Unsurprisingly, you can purchase armour sets, weaponry and various other bits and bobs from the store, with two kinds of currency, one premium in the shape of Arcs, while the other, Dracs, can be earned in-game. There’s also plenty to find and equip from defeating enemies and exploring dungeons out in the world. If you’re coming from Warframe, you’ll know that Digital Extremes are not the kind of company to nickel and dime players, and I’d expect that you can play the entire game without spending a penny. That’s a good deal, whatever your expectations, but Soulframe looks as though it’ll more than meet them.

Soulframe already feels like a meaningful and worthy update to the Warframe formula, with a setting that begs to be explored and experienced. Fortunately, PC players will be able to dive into the Preludes open beta from Friday, 6th November.

items.title: Devstream 198 Overview
items.summary: With Warframe: Tau launching later this year, our first of two dedicated Devstreams took you deeper into its new Star Chart than ever before. We showcased Brysko's Abilities along with his brutal new Weapons, as well as his Chimera Skin — t
items.content:
With Warframe: Tau launching later this year, our first of two dedicated Devstreams took you deeper into its new Star Chart than ever before.

We showcased Brysko's Abilities along with his brutal new Weapons, as well as his Chimera Skin — the first in a new class of elite Customizations. We also moved beyond Fornax to the wastelands of Perita, where allies are scarce amongst the warring desert clans battling it out for the moon's precious resources. Be sure to join us next month for our second, Tau-focused Devstream where we'll have even more surprises in store!

Catch up on everything we showcased with our official Overview!

items.title: Soulframe to launch into free open beta this week, as Warframe devs go head-to-head with WoW: Forever
items.summary: Soulframe's new update will allow anyone who wants to to jump into the game, refreshes the onboarding with a vast corrupted map, and adds a Pact to unlock.
items.content:
Image credit: Digital Extremes News by Connor Makar Reporter Published on Nov. 2, 2026, 11:17 a.m. 10 comments Follow Soulframe Prioritise us on Google Soulframe's Preludes (its own version of a beta) is finally opening its doors to the whole world ahead of the Verse of the Veilands update. Starting this week, anyone who wants to can simply download the game and hop in, no invite required.

The date this happens is an interesting one: 6th November. That's two days after the release of World of Warcraft: Forever and the same week as Old School RuneScape 's Hardcore worlds, so it's suddenly become a pretty packed month for MMO enthusiasts.

This comes after three years of closed testing for the fantasy action MMORPG, which players have been able to gradually see firsthand through sporadic invites. With Soulframe suffering delays since its first reveal, brief invite events have already occurred over this period. Even locked away, the game has received multiple substantial updates over the years, including new quests, Pacts (classes), factions and so on.

As for what newcomers to Soulframe can look forward to when Soulframe opens its doors, the Verse of the Veillands update is bringing a total overhaul of the map progression system this month. After the completion of an early quest, players are introduced to a corrupted landscape, the Veillands, which they must purify.

As you do so, new resources will be obtainable and side activities like fishing will be unlocked. You'll also be able to train up a small wolf pet into a full-on mount in the process. Previously, players were just thrust into the open world to explore and figure things out as they go, so this should provide something of an introduction to the game's open map. It won't be totally finished when released mind you, with updates to the Veillands system coming in the future.

On top of that, there's a new Pact called the Ode Shrike coming with the update. It's a tricksy trapper with spikes, balloon snares, bombs and chains to disrupt enemies as you whittle them down.

Could this be enough to win people over to Digital Extreme's newest project? Time will tell - but in the meantime its long-lasting sci-fi MMO Warframe is taking players to the Tau system in a major next step in the game's narrative this December. It comes with a detective noir inspired main quest, playable warframe, and even an in-universe Poker equivalent.

items.title: Warframe officially adds a whole new star system in December
items.summary: Warframe will leave the Origin System and head to Tau before the end of the year
items.content:
By Tomas Franzese Published Oct 31, 2026, 10:58 AM EDT Tomas Franzese is the Weekend News Editor at Polygon, following and reporting on the latest goings-on in the gaming and entertainment spaces. During the week, you can find him working on Remastered , his newsletter about video game history and retro gaming, or contributing to GameSpot and other publications. Previously, Tomas was the Gaming Segment Lead at XDA and a Staff Writer at Digital Trends . News Warframe will leave the Origin System and head to Tau before the end of the year

Image: Digital Extremes Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Warframe Sign in to your Polygon.com account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Before the end of the year, Warframe will get a whole lot bigger . The Warframe: Tau expansion will be released for free in December and adds its namesake star system to the live service shooter alongside a lot of other new content.

Digital Extremes finally confirmed the Dec. 2026 release window for Warframe: Tau during Devstream 198 on Oct. 30. That stream also showed more of the expansion, which we first got a glimpse of at TennoCon earlier this year. While almost all of Warframe has taken place in the Origin System for the past thirteen years, this expansion finally adds a new star system that's been referenced within the game's lore for some time.

The expansion adds a new single-player chapter and introduces players to the game's 67th playable Warframe. He's named Brysko, voiced by Matt Mercer , and inspired by noir detective characters. Players can earn him for free through gameplay, but they can also instantly buy and unlock Brysko in the Warframe Market.

Once players wrap up the new story chapter, they'll be able to explore and complete missions in two Tau system locations, Perita and Fornax. A dedicated Tau System Star Chart will serve as the hub for all this new content. New cosmetics for Koumei and Nezha are also in the works, as is plenty of future content meant to flesh out what's available to players in Tau.

While the more imminent updates for Warframe will focus primarily on Tau, Digital Extremes Community Director Megan Everett stressed in a press release that the developers aren't abandoning the Origin Systems. "To all our players, new and returning, the Origin System is not being left behind," Everett explained. "While we focus right now on Tau, we have so many stories to tell, and now just have more places to share them.”

Warframe: Tau launches across all platforms that the sci-fi shooter is available on in December. It'll be a busy end of the year for Digital Extremes, as we recently learned that Soulframe Open Preludes will open up access to everyone on Nov. 6.

items.title: Warframe: Tau Will Officially Be Released in December 2026
items.summary: New details have been revealed for Warframe: Tau, bringing the new Warframe Brysko, voiced by Matthew Mercer, and more this December.
items.content:
Posted in: Digital Extremes , Games , Video Games , Warframe | Tagged: Warframe: Tau

New details have been revealed for Warframe: Tau, bringing the new Warframe Brysko, voiced by Matthew Mercer, and more this December.

Digital Extremes revealed all of the new content coming soon for Warframe: Tau , the latest expansion of the game that will cap off a pretty successful 2026 for the game. The content will arrive sometime in December 2026, but a date has not yet been set. Within it, you'll travel to a new star system, get a new Warframe with Brysko, a ton of cosmetics, and more. Plus, they will be launching a new card game based on the video game. We have the dev notes below, along with images and the recent dev video.

Venture to a new Star System, Tau, and discover a new single-player cinematic narrative chapter, unlocking new variants of cooperative gameplay modes, including a revamped Survival mission on the Fornax moon, Perita, to squad up with friends online. All for free, on all major console and PC platforms.

Step beyond the Origin System and enter a paradise lost to war and ruin. A brand-new Star Chart is filled with new forces, friends and foes, and so much to discover. The Old Peace (Dec. 2025) update introduced players to what Tau once was, and Warframe: Tau (Dec. 2026) will unearth what has become following eons of conflict, with a first look at present-day Perita and the hostile forces overseeing this decayed wasteland.

Perita will debut with Warframe: Tau in December alongside the mob-run ring city of Fornax as two distinct locations, on which players will discover new stories and challenges while Tau evolves with each following update. Take a trip down to MANIFOLD 90-BF, a new social hub on the mafia-riddled Fornax full of new characters, rivals, and lore secrets to uncover. Cut through the chaos of the Perita to encounter The Cleaving Glaive, a new ally Syndicate scavenging the Perita wasteland in search of Tau secrets.

The 67th Warframe, Brysko, will be available to all Warframe players and can be instantly unlocked from the Warframe Market or earned through gameplay when Warframe: Tau arrives in December. Voiced by legendary actor Matthew Mercer ( Final Fantasy VII: Revelation, The Legend of Vox Machina ) in a curious inner monologue, Brysko draws on the detective noir genre and serves as the protagonist of the single-player cinematic narrative Quest players will discover when Warframe: Tau arrives. Brysko leads the charge in an all-new cosmetic class in Warframe – the Chimera Skin. Players were treated to a deep dive into Brysko's ability kit and gameplay mechanics, showcasing his Hound companion, signature gear like his Rain & Shine fist weapons, and his Exalted magnum — Corecracker.

Weave the strands of destiny with the dice maiden Koumei's first-ever Deluxe Skin release, Koumei Enshoujo. A first look at Koumei's avant-garde cosmetic design was showcased live in-game ahead of her femme fatale release alongside Warframe: Tau in December. The mercurial firemonger Nezha is next in line for the Warframe Heirloom Skin treatment, with a first look at concept art revealed. Co-designed with Mati Tapia and Stephan Sotelting of Sumo Digital and Digital Extremes, players won't want to miss out on this one-of-a-kind skin arriving in early 2027.

Raise the stakes for board game night with the new Portau Card Collection and Portau Playmat, now available for pre-order from the Official Warframe Merch Store. Tune in to Digital Extremes' Princess Margaret Foundation Cancer Quest finale stream Saturday, Oct. 31 at 12 p.m. ET on Warframe's Twitch and YouTube channels to watch the team and some very special guests face off in an all-out Portau tournament.

items.summary: Verse of the Veilands will radically change the structure of the game so it
items.content:
RPG Soulframe opens up for everyone next week as the Warframe devs prepare the fantasy action RPG for one of its 'biggest, most violent' updates ever next month News By Tyler Colp Published 30 October 2026 Verse of the Veilands will radically change the structure of the game so it's easier for new players to follow.

If you've been waiting to see what the developers of Warframe are doing with a fantasy action RPG, you'll finally be able to jump in and see for yourself.

The transition to an open alpha will be followed by a massive transformation to the structure of the game later in November. Midrath, Soulframe's big open landmass, won't be the verdant, almost chill, place it used to be: The entire area will be corrupted and it's your job to bring it back to life. "You're going to enter a game that is much more unforgiving and harsh at first glance," creative director Geoff Crookes explained in a recent presentation attended by PC Gamer.

This update, Prelude 17 or Verse of the Veillands, is a huge shift for Soulframe, but an important one that will help new players acclimate to the world. Crookes said the goal is to improve the onboarding experience and to give players "much more ownership" over their decisions early on. It won't be fully finished yet, however, so what's in there today is just "the functional bones" of what will come in the final game.

Feedback from players who struggled to reach the point of the game where they could freely explore the open world convinced the team there needed to be a more direct intro. In Verse of the Veilands, the main quest will teach you how to stop the siphons draining the world of its color. Enemies and resources you encounter will change as each zone is restored and side activities, like fishing, will become available. You'll also be able to raise a wolf pup into a full-on mount.

"The system is also helping the worldbuilding," Crookes said. Pages and pages of new writing for each faction leader will be added and you'll start to hear them radio in and fill you in on the history of the world. The team said it wants them to have a more "integrated" role in your journey as you work to cleanse Midrath of the corruption.

Despite the tragic death of its lead writer, one of the scariest games I have ever played will finally come out later this month Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter

A new Pact, Soulframe's equivalent of a class (or a Warframe), will be added, too. The name of it was still undecided during the presentation, but the developers described it as a "hunter, poacher-type Pact" related to the alien Ode race. Equipping it will let you tie enemies together with a sci-fi bola, pierce them with a cone of spikes, and send them flying away by attaching a giant balloon to them à la Metal Gear Solid 5.

The developers stressed that there's a lot packed into Verse of the Veilands, so much so that they were still tweaking things days before the presentation. Crookes and McGregor nervously expressed that it would "hopefully" be done in time for today, but it seems it won't quite make it in time. That said, the plan is for the update to be out before the end of the next month, so new players might want to wait until then.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"I think this is probably one of the biggest, most violent changes we've made to the structure of the game in a long while," lead designer Scott McGregor said. "Paired with open Preludes is nerve-wracking and we hope players and the feedback stays positive."

The final (final_vfinal_finalfinal.exe) version of everything in Verse of the Veilands will be shown during a stream later today on the Soulframe Twitch channel .

items.title: Warframe: Tau Coming In December
items.summary: Your remarkable journey is about to lead to an era-defining trip to the Tau System, where new worlds ripe for exploration are waiting. Jump back into Warframe today and get ready to experience our most expansive update ever this December. 6
items.content:
Your remarkable journey is about to lead to an era-defining trip to the Tau System, where new worlds ripe for exploration are waiting. Jump back into Warframe today and get ready to experience our most expansive update ever this December.

67TH WARFRAME: BRYSKO

Hit the streets of Fornax as Brysko, the world-weary, noir-inspired detective brought to life with an inner monologue voiced by Matt Mercer. Enforce your own brand of street justice with an indomitable suite of Abilities, trusty Hound Companion and signature armaments like the Rain & Shine Fist Weapons and Corecracker Exalted Pistol. Brysko also introduces the first in a new class of premium Customizations: the Chimera Skin. As with a Protoframe, you'll be able to switch between his Warframe and Chimera aspects on the fly for a more Sentient appearance and voice-acted dialogue.

TAU STAR CHART

Your evolution continues in a new region of space beyond anything you've ever known: the Tau System. While there will remain much to do in the Origin System going forward, you'll also be able to enter Missions and explore new worlds across Tau. December will start you off with the mob-run ring city of Fornax, as well as the badlands of Perita, with many more planned for future updates.

PERITA

Although Perita thrived following the events of The Old Peace, its ecosystem has since collapsed into a hostile desert populated by feuding clans of Dazannah — and where both resources and allies are notoriously difficult to come by. With the last unconquered clan facing existential peril, its chieftain’s young son, Catulast, seeks help from its ancient foe, the Tenno. Will you brave the wasteland and answer its call?

items.title: Nidus Prime and Saryn Prime Enter Prime Resurgence

items.content:
Harness Nidus Prime’s relentless mutations or spread deadly toxins across the battlefield with Saryn Prime. Add this deleterious duo, along with their signature Prime Weapons and Prime Accessories, to your Arsenal today with Regal Aya.

Nidus Prime

A relentless embodiment of the Infestation, Nidus Prime thrives in the chaos of the battle, growing stronger with every mutation. Harness his parasitic powers to ensnare enemies, unleash devastating attacks and bolster his own survivability. With no conventional shields to rely on, Nidus Prime is an excellent choice for Tenno who prefer an aggressive, ability-driven playstyle that rewards you the longer you stay in the fight.

Saryn Prime

A deadly plague given form, Saryn Prime spreads toxic devastation across the battlefield, leaving few enemies untouched. Infect foes with corrosive spores, empower your weapons with lethal toxins and unleash waves of viral destruction upon entire groups. Her exceptional area-of-effect damage makes her an excellent choice for Tenno who enjoy overwhelming enemies and clearing large crowds with ease.

Prime Warframes

Check out our guide to Prime Warframes video for a helpful breakdown of what Prime Warframes are, different ways you can earn them and how you can purchase Prime items.

items.title: 5 Best Video Games Like Warframe
items.summary: If you dig the action in "Warframe" and are looking for something that will give you an analogous experience, check out these five games.
items.content:
Digital Extremes Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Warframe" is a video game that has stood the test of time for over a decade and continues to reward its loyal player base with fresh content, updates, and support. The game can't really be tethered to a single genre either, as it's an MMO, RPG, sci-fi-based story adventure, and looter shooter all wrapped up into a single package. While this makes the game feel accessible to a wide variety of players, it can also make it difficult for players to compare "Warframe" to any other game on offer.

Fortunately, some titles out there share one or more similarities with "Warframe" and can give you a comparable experience. While these titles might not be free-to-play and possess thousands of hours of content like "Warframe," they have at least one shared feature with the game that makes you feel like stepping into the suit of your Tenno all over again. Below, you'll find five games similar to "Warframe" and why fans might enjoy playing them.

Bungie "Destiny 2" is arguably the closest comparison to "Warframe" available in 2026. Both games are MMOs set in a sci-fi world with plenty of emphasis on developing the story. Not only that, but you'll also find that "Destiny 2" shares plenty of the same core elements as "Warframe," including collecting vast amounts of loot, selecting and customizing your character's class, and completing missions in co-op multiplayer. While it might sound like "Destiny 2" isn't anything different from "Warframe," that's not the case in the slightest, as the two play very differently, gameplay-wise.

"Destiny 2" is a fast-paced first-person shooter with a more challenging combat system that demands strategy and mastery over your weapons and skills. Raids present the most difficult challenge in the game, as these are large-scale events that reward a ton of loot, but there's plenty of individual content to take part in as well. Just like "Warframe," you can engage with this content as a solo player or in a party, and there are both PvE and PvP elements across a variety of modes and events. The two games might not play exactly the same, but "Destiny 2" is your best bet if you want something with all of the features that make "Warframe" great. However, it should be noted that developer Bungie has announced major changes to the future of "Destiny 2," which has caused a dip in player count.

Arrowhead Game Studios Compared to "Warframe," "Helldivers 2" offers a totally different experience from top to bottom. While both games have a sci-fi setting and feature co-op functionality, "Helldivers 2" doesn't really fall into any of the genres that define "Warframe." Instead, the game is a unique action-adventure experience that takes teamwork to a whole new level. "Helldivers 2" can't be played solo and requires four players to be in a party nearly at all times.

With your party, which can be comprised of friends or strangers that you match with, you'll drop into specific missions that are taking place all over a galaxy on different planets. You have various objectives you need to complete on these planets and a certain amount of time to extract before you fail the mission. When you're completing objectives, some of which are nearly impossible to finish , you can use a predefined loadout that you set before a drop starts. Your loadout can consist of weapons, gear, and special abilities that you unlock the further you progress. "Helldivers 2" is an entirely interactive and unique experience that doesn't offer the same narrative aspect as "Warframe," but its gameplay loop is highly rewarding.

NEXON "The First Descendant" is the only game on this list that primarily follows the "Warframe" model of being a free-to-play MMO looter shooter. While "The First Descendant" features far more monetization, the two games have a very similar gameplay style that "Warframe" fans will immediately recognize and be able to hop into. From the third-person perspective to the character customization to the overwhelming number of cosmetics, there's a lot to like if you're a "Warframe" fan.

Even the settings of the two games are similar, as "The First Descendant" takes place in a sci-fi universe where your character has enhanced abilities and travels to all sorts of different planets during the story. However, there's not a huge emphasis on the story, as "The First Descendant" is more about the loot grind than anything else. To obtain most rare pieces of gear, you need to research their designs, and you can do that by acquiring blueprints from various bosses and objectives. This can be a huge time commitment, though, as "The First Descendant" can have you repeating a boss for days before you get the drop you want.

Blizzard Entertainment From a strictly gameplay perspective, "Warframe" and "Diablo 4" are extremely different. One is a fast-paced third-person shooter MMO, while the other is a top-down ARPG with distinct character classes that alter your entire playstyle. However, if you take a look under the hood, "Diablo 4" has plenty to like if you're a "Warframe" fan.

For starters, "Diablo 4" places an enormous emphasis on loot, as every enemy and boss you kill has a chance to drop some rare piece of gear. While guns don't play a role in the loot, you can obtain weapons, such as staves or melee weapons, as well as jewelry and armor with certain traits that boost your character's abilities. "Diablo 4" also has an excellent base campaign filled with unique open-world zones, tough bosses, and progression. While you can also take on one of the several expansion campaigns, you can also engage in some PvP or the endgame grind that focuses on improving your loot and stats. Getting past the top-down view and alternate RPG mechanics might be hard at first for "Warframe" players, but "Diablo 4" is worth learning some new playstyles.

2K Arguably the most influential franchise in the entire looter shooter genre is "Borderlands," which helped define the genre back when the original game was released in 2009. While you could play any of the "Borderlands" games for a top-notch looter shooter experience, "Borderlands 4" is the most recent entry in the franchise. You don't need to play any of the previous games in the series to understand what's going on, either, so you can just hop right in.

Aside from the focus on looting, "Borderlands 4" and "Warframe" are both story-driven RPGs with open worlds and deep character progression. "Borderlands 4" can also be played with friends, as the series has been regarded as one of the best co-op experiences ever . However, there are more differences than similarities between the two games, as "Borderlands 4" is a first-person shooter with no PvP whatsoever. That said, the game is still an incredible experience, as you have a huge world to explore, vehicles to ride, and more loot than you'll ever know what to do with. It also features plenty of edgy dialogue and cutscenes, which often lead to some outrageous moments in both the main story and side quests. So, if you're looking for a witty and fun looter shooter RPG to hop into after a "Warframe" session, "Borderlands 4" certainly fits the bill.

items.summary: The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for y
items.content:
The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for your listening pleasure on major streaming platforms. "Devourer," was first heard during the Epoch Operation: Taubound Official Gameplay Teaser. Influenced by slow, heavy metal from the likes of Black Sabbath, it features lyrics "sung" in Voidtongue, the terrifyingly enigmatic language of the Untime. This was a deliberate choice, recalling the memorable moment from 2023's Whispers in the Walls Quest when you took control of one of Albrecht Entrati's Vessels for the first time. Here, these elements combine for a musical experience that feels as massive and imposing as your latest endeavors ahead of Warframe: Tau, coming later this year.

  • Apple Music

items.title: I Underestimated The New Icebind Game Mode in Warframe – Opinion
items.summary: The new Icebind game mode in Warframe is an excellent new idea that finally launched after being delayed, here is a critique of it.
items.content:
A couple of days ago, I wrote an article venting my frustrations and disappointment in the recent update in Warframe , the Iceblade of Narin. Having the grind for her and her weapons locked to already existing game modes with their own loot pools, bloating the drop chances, felt like a miss to me. All the while, the way it was the send-off update before we ramp up for Tau felt a little underwhelming overall. In a recent update, Digital Extremes added the endgame game mode that was delayed, the “Icebind,” and it fixes one problem I had listed in that previous article, and another longstanding issue with Digital Extremes’ approach to endgame content, while also adding a few issues of its own.

The Icebind is the newest game mode in Warframe that was originally delayed from the Iceblade of Narin update . It is a 6-player, endgame-focused activity that requires manually inviting people to do it. The Icebind has 4 different game modes you can choose from, including:

How this game mode differs is set modifiers and very harsh conditions, including enemies at level 999 and above. As well as only allows one player to use a specific warframe in the squad. This means that you cannot stack 5 Dantes and a Harrow to avoid every harsh condition. This game mode also opts for additional side objectives that, if you start and fail, you fail the mission overall. Completing the side objectives gives you extra keys to acquire loot at the end of the mission.

With all of this out in the open, how does this game mode actually land? Well, I think it lands very well on its own two feet and feels much more rewarding and enjoyable as opposed to the weekly Archimedea runs that have become feeling a little outdated. It is a refresh of the endgame approach for Warframe and one that is definitely welcome, so long as there are aims to improve it.

The Icebind puts 6 players into already existing game modes with side objectives, when I feel the new objectives could have been their own game modes altogether. The side objectives are an interesting mix of new ideas. For example, players have to stand in a line to link up power from one place to another. A giant ice shrine you need to do a lot of DPS to break the bubbles around it. Not to mention a bubble that marks areas around it that are safe and unsafe to jump around to avoid getting hit. And a chest that requires keys dropped by enemies to open by standing next to said chest.

They do not sound really interesting on their own, but they are fun in practice so long as players understand what they are doing. My biggest concern about the integration here is how these new objectives are just optional challenges in already existing game modes when they feel like they could have been mixed into one game mode that goes from one step to the next. For example, the power chain being the opening objective, then the orb with the little “Simon says” area around it following the chain, then leading into that DPS check with the ice shrine before needing to do the chest as the final objective to unlock extraction.

Obviously, I know making these objectives optional in the existing game modes made it easier for players to engage in. But if there are going to be more experimentation for endgame content with this type of stuff, a dedication to the new ideas as opposed to old ones would be a better way to go, to me at least. This game mode does correct one issue in the overall update, however. That being how Narin is integrated into the wider narrative.

In my previous article critiquing the general update, I mentioned how there was a complete absence of narrative integration for Narin. I was not aware that the integration would be worked into the Icebind, instead of a dedicated mission for when you are farming for Narin. It’s a subversion that I wasn’t expecting, but I do understand what Digital Extremes were going for now. The only little bit of inconsistency is the lack of the murmur.

Seeing as the Icebind makes references to the Hex and the Indifference worming its way further into the origin system. I feel the murmur should have been the only enemy for narrative cohesion. As it stands, however, it is better worked in now, and I feel better about the update overall. I do look forward to hearing more explanations as the weeks progress with the Icebind.

Finally, the rewards are weirdly misrepresented. When the rewards were shown off originally, I assumed stuff like the Kuva were going to be bad-luck RNG drops. As some of us know from sorties/archon hunts. Luckily, that is not the case. Every chest drops a random good item, like boosters, rivens, forma, etc on top of the Kuva. My only complaint about this system is having a singular forma in the same drop table as a forma bundle. Not to mention the Kuva amount from either drop feels low. I think adding some entropic Kuva to the drop tables would incentivise players more to get the cosmetics and other goodies from Melica.

Finally, the new Riven Splicers are great. I have zero complaints about how they function. I also appreciate that they are a guaranteed reward on top of everything earned in an Icebind run. This feature is an excellent overhaul to the Riven system for endgame players. Heck, my negative crit Phenmor riven has weak spot damage now. Which is a fantastically nasty combo with my Harrow.

With all of this out in the open. I would like to recommend that Digital Extremes keep going with this idea. I feel the Icebind is strangely more approachable than Archimedea right now. This is mostly due to the fact that they do not force you to play with frames and weapons you do not like or have proper builds for. Enticing players to use their best-of-the-best builds and weapons for singular mission runs is a great idea. I just feel like the objectives could be their own things. As well as touching up the reward pool for better consistency. As it stands, just asking for an Icebind group in recruitment chat or in Yuvan Peak works perfectly.

items.title: October in Warframe
items.summary: As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following e
items.content:
As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following events this month:

EPOCH OPERATION: TAUBOUND

October 15 - November 17 A unique event unlike anything you've experienced to date, Epoch Operation: Taubound offers all eligible Tenno the chance to become a part of Warframe history. If you want to help open up a path to the Tau System, be sure to have your account ready by completing the "Vor's Prize" Quest before October 15. Players looking to pilot their Vessel for the first time can also complete The Hex and The Old Peace in order to access a new, permanent Prologue Quest setting up the Road to Tau. For full event details – including prerequisites and more – click here.

NIGHTS OF NABERUS

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Spooky season returns to the Origin System during our annual Halloween-inspired event, with Daughter releasing her inventory of new and returning seasonal Customizations in exchange for Mother Tokens. While Baro Ki'Teer will mark the occasion in the same unsettling fashion as last year (IYKYK), we're also mixing it up by bringing back the Hallowed Nightmares Tactical Alert, allowing you to face off against the fearsome Jack O'Naut for even more Naberus treats. For all the harrowing details, check out our Halloween 2026 Events post.

NEW GAME MODE: THE ICEBIND

October 7 Originally intended to ship alongside Iceblade of Narin as "Glacial Defiance," our new 6-player game mode was ultimately delayed to allow for additional development time and renamed to The Icebind. Accessible in-game starting October 7, these challenging, high-level Missions can be played up to three times weekly, allowing you to put your teamwork (and Loadouts) to the test for valuable Rewards. Visit the official Warframe Forums to learn more about the delay, and further details of the game mode itself.

PRINCESS MARGARET CANCER FOUNDATION QUEST

October 1 - October 31 PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation light the way towards a world free from the fear of cancer. Visit the Warframe PMCF Quest webpage for more information or donate directly here.
